title: Ethene (C₂H₄) — Planar Double Bonds
description: Investigate unsaturated alkenes, Sp2 hybridization, and why double bonds lock atoms into a flat plane.

steps.prompt: Ethene contains a C=C double bond. How does the double bond affect rotation of the CH₂ groups around the carbon-carbon axis?
options: Free rotation like a spinning propeller
Rigid / locked in a single flat plane
steps.explanation: Correct! The pi (π) bond in the double bond requires sideways overlap of unhybridized p-orbitals, preventing free rotation and locking all 6 atoms into a single plane.

steps.prompt: Rotate the ethene molecule so you view it edge-on. Confirm that all six atoms align along a flat sheet.
steps.explanation: Sp2 hybridization produces trigonal planar geometry around each carbon with bond angles very close to 120°.

steps.prompt: What chemical test distinguishes unsaturated hydrocarbons like ethene from saturated alkanes?
options: Burning with a soot-free clear blue flame
steps.explanation: Ethene readily undergoes addition reactions across its double bond, quickly decolorizing bromine water from red-brown to colorless.
